title: Coherent complex presentation of a canonical derived pullback cocone
statement: Let $I$ be a small cofiltered category, $T$ a scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $D:I\to\mathrm{Scheme}$ a diagram, $c$ a cone with point $Y$, $t:D\to T$ a compatible family of structure maps, and $p:Y\to T$ with $\pi_i t_i=p$. Let $K\in D(\mathrm{Ab}(T_{\mathrm{et}}))$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], $C$ a complex on $T$, and $q:K\simeq QC$. Fix an integer $n$, a diagram $H:I^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Ab}$, and a cocone $B$ whose objects, transition maps and legs are identified with the derived pullback cohomology of $K$ by object isomorphisms $e_i,e_Y$ and the canonical adjunction-unit, Leray and inverse-image composition formulas [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology, lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition]. Let $P(f,A)$ be the canonical complex cohomology pullback, namely cohomology of derived global sections of the derived adjunction unit, followed by the Leray comparison and the exact-functor localization factorization [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Then there are complexes $C_i=t_i^{-1}C$, maps $\phi_f:f^{-1}C_i\to C_j$ satisfying the identity and composition laws, and isomorphisms $eG_i:p^{-1}C\simeq\pi_i^{-1}C_i$ identifying their transitions with the identity of the constant diagram $G=\mathrm{const}(p^{-1}C)$. With $L$ the identity cocone of $G$, there are isomorphisms $eH_i:H_i\simeq H^n(D_i,QC_i)$ and $eB:B\simeq H^n(Y,QL)$ such that $H(f)=eH_i\,P(D(f),C_i)\,H^n(Q\phi_f)\,eH_j^{-1}$ and $B_i\,eB=eH_i\,P(\pi_i,C_i)\,H^n(Q(eG_i^{-1}L_i))$. These are the fields of ComplexPullbackPresentation. No boundedness, geometric limit, qcqs or affine-transition assumption is made and no cohomology colimit is asserted.

proof.text: Choose A_i as the termwise pullback of C, phi as the inverse comparison, and eG as the comparison along each projection. Obtain their unit, composition, and cone equations from the geometric coherence theorem. The concrete identity comparison is named presentationIdentityMap with its source and target explicit; unfolding it recovers the original field exactly.

Define eH_i and eB by composing the given object identifications with cohomology of inverse image q and the exact-functor factorization. Apply single-triangle transport to each D(f) and cancel eH_j to identify hH. Apply it to each projection and cancel eY to identify hB. Assemble all twelve fields of the presentation.
